Label anatomy · 2026-09-17

What a training label is, and what the model is asked to predict

query pixel, given to the modellabel cut point10–20 mm admissible intervalpetiole centreline, 4–30 mm from the junctiontarget petiole instance maskmodel prediction

How the label is built

  1. Each plant asset carries a 3-D centreline polyline (with radius) for every petiole, its attachment point on the main stem, and the parent link. The green mask is that petiole's instance segmentation in the rendered frame.
  2. The cut point is the centreline point 10 mm from the stem attachment toward the leaves; the admissible interval is the same centreline from 10 to 20 mm. Both are projected into the head camera with the exact intrinsics and robot pose, to sub-pixel precision (magenta and yellow).
  3. The query pixel is a point on the same petiole's centreline at least 45 mm from the attachment and 18 px from the cut, chosen from the visible part of the mask and screened for size, contrast and exposure (white). Its distance along the petiole varies per sample so a fixed query-to-cut offset cannot be learned.
  4. Visible label: the 4–30 mm neighbourhood of the junction is ≥95% visible in the mask and depth, and the query connects to the cut through visible petiole pixels → answer = the magenta point. Occluded label: a foreground leaf, fruit or stem is positively identified over the cut region → answer = abstain; the hidden cut location is stored but never given to the model or the scorer. Ambiguous cases are excluded, not labelled.

The 10 mm rule is a versioned engineering convention (petiole_arc_10_20mm_prototype.v1), agreed but not yet horticulturally validated. The label is exactly where the rule says on the true petiole; whether that is where a grower would cut is a separate question.
